_why: The registry of exceptions to tools/check-living-years.py, which fails when a birth year or date on or after the living line (this year minus 80) is printed for a person with no death beside it. Three kinds of entry, nothing else. unpublished_deaths: a person the archive's own data records as dead (a death in the chart's working files, a burial register row, a headstone transcription) whose own page does not print the death. They are NOT living by the rule and their births are not masked, but nobody has confirmed the death for publication, and no tool adds one: David confirms each, and the entry is deleted when the death is recorded on the page (or the person is found to be living and goes on data/living-roster.tsv). snippets: one stated piece of text in one file, with the reason it is not a living person's birth. spellings: other forms a dead person's name is written in, so that a birth beside one of them is recognised as theirs (the kit's gate does not read this key; check-living-years.py does). On 25 October 2026 David confirmed the six people the registry held as unpublished deaths (Gayle, Jeffrey, Paul Raymond, Catherine Tersia, Jeanette Marie, Patricia Carmen) as dead; each death is now printed on the person's page and the list is empty. A name is never added here to silence the gate. also_written: other spellings the sources use for the same registered person (so a birth written under them is recognised as theirs); a form is only honoured when the birth year beside it is within three of the year the data holds.

spellings.reason: Catherine Tersia Lerena, written Catherine Tertia and Karon (her married name) in the 1971 notice and the commercial index; her page prints her death, so a birth beside any of these forms is hers and is excused only within three years of the one the data holds.
